---
title: "Case study: butterfly monitoring in the Wanang forest plot"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev.args = list(bg = "white"),
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 150, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4
)
```

Luk et al. (2019) counted butterflies on 36 days, three a month over 12
months spread across three years, in the Wanang forest dynamics plot,
Papua New Guinea. Repeated sampling of one place suits questions about
temporal diversity: how much does a year of monitoring capture, and how
different are years?

**Source and licence.** Data on Dryad (doi:10.5061/dryad.j35fq7r) under
CC0 1.0. Only the Wanang part of the published multi-site data is
included. See `?wanang_butterflies` and `data-raw/wanang_butterflies.R`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(2026)
wanang_butterflies
```

## Each year of monitoring

Pooling the days within each year gives one sample per year:

```{r years}
years <- mutate(wanang_butterflies, site = paste("Year", year))
div_coverage(years)
div_estimate(years, nboot = 100)
```

Each year recorded more than 4000 butterflies with coverage above 99%, yet
estimated richness exceeds observed richness by about 20 to 50 species: rare
species remain undetected after a full year.

```{r curves, fig.alt = "Butterfly rarefaction and extrapolation curves for each year"}
autoplot(div_rarefy(years, q = c(0, 1, 2), knots = 40, nboot = 100))
```

## How different are the years?

```{r beta}
beta_multi(years)
```

Most of the difference between years is turnover. Within each year, the
four sampled months also differ substantially:

```{r months}
wanang_butterflies |>
  mutate(site = paste("Month", month)) |>
  beta_multi(.by = year)
```

These results support the paper's conclusion that monitoring across
several years captures far more of the species pool than any single year.

## Reference

Luk, C.-L., Basset, Y., Kongnoo, P., Hau, B. C. H. and Bonebrake, T. C.
(2019). Inter-annual monitoring improves diversity estimation of tropical
butterfly assemblages. *Biotropica*, 51, 519-528. doi:10.1111/btp.12671
